tasks.short: Explain techniques and safety procedures and demonstrate equipment to participants, prepare safety instruction cards, and record that participants received the safety instruction.

steps.what: Recreation worker explains principles, techniques and safety procedures and demonstrates use of equipment
Recreation worker prepares safety instruction cards
Recreation worker records that participants received the safety instruction: on a paper list today, by a tick on the booking list after the change

tasks.design: Safety instruction cards per activity are kept in a shared library ({DOCS}) so workers print or show them instead of making their own. The booking system's participant list ({OTHER}) has a tick box for safety instruction received, replacing the paper list. Explaining and demonstrating stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each worker made own cards and kept paper lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared libraries and booking lists with tick boxes are easy to set up.
tasks.still_hard: Participants do not read safety cards.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the participant who did not understand the instruction.

reach.learn: Whether safety instruction is recorded for every participant.

evidence.claim: Shared libraries and booking lists with tick boxes are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from the activity session to instruction recorded; activity design is outside.
Input contract: cards kept by the activity manager; fallback is own cards and paper lists.

Explaining and demonstrating keep their full time. s2 keeps 50 because the worker still picks, adapts and prints cards from the library. s3 keeps 40 because the names come from the booking list; the worker still ticks each participant.
research_questions: Is safety instruction recorded for every participant?

incremental.description: Recreation worker suggests updates to shared cards.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library covers few activities and many participants are walk-ins not on the booking list (3.0); high: cards exist for most activities and most participants book (7.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the special activity or event, handle participant registrations, check the programme and participant information, send the information to participants, and direct the event on the day.

steps.what: Recreation worker plans the special activity or event
Participants register online for the event in the booking system
Recreation worker handles participant registrations: by phone and e-mail today; after the change only phone bookings and questions
Recreation worker checks the final event information: programme, times, place and what to bring, and that it goes to the participants on the list
Recreation worker sends the checked event information to participants: by e-mails today, by one send from the booking system after the change
Recreation worker directs the special activity or event, such as aquatics or performing arts

tasks.design: Events start from a checklist template per event type ({DOCS}) with staffing, equipment and safety items. Participants register online in the booking system ({OTHER}), which keeps the list and capacity, instead of the worker taking calls and e-mails. The worker checks the final information and the list, then sends it once to all participants from the booking system. Directing the event stays with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were made from scratch and registrations taken by phone and e-mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking systems take online registrations and send participant messages.
tasks.still_hard: Weather and late changes upset plans.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a group of nervous children calm before a show.

reach.learn: Whether more people register in time.

evidence.claim: Booking systems take online registrations, track capacity and message participants.

assumptions: Boundary: from the event request to the event held; event budgets are outside.
Input contract: templates kept by the team; fallback is phone and e-mail registration.
Participants register online (s2p, share 1) in about the time a call took; this is customer time outside the worker's savings.

Directing the event and checking the information keep their full time. s1 keeps 70 because the template lists standard staffing, equipment and safety items; the plan itself is still the worker's. s2 keeps 30 for phone bookings and questions. s4 keeps 20 for the send itself.

incremental.description: Recreation worker sets up each event in the booking system.

approvals.approved_version: The event information with programme, times and place exactly as checked by the worker in s3, sent once from the booking system to the participants registered for this event; any change needs a new check and send.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: small events where most people still phone, and the template fits little (9.8); high: most participants register online and the template fits (19.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make the duty roster, assign duties at the start of the day, train new staff, supervise staff during activities, and handle shift swaps.

steps.what: Staff enter their availability in the scheduling app
Recreation worker makes the duty roster: in a spreadsheet today; after the change the app proposes it from availability and rules and the worker adjusts it
Recreation worker checks the final roster: every activity covered by staff with the right skills, contract hours and rest times kept, and a fair spread of duties
Recreation worker publishes the checked roster to the staff in the scheduling app
Recreation worker assigns work duties at the start of the day
Recreation worker trains new staff members
Recreation worker supervises personnel during activities
Recreation worker handles shift swap requests by message

tasks.design: Staff enter availability in a scheduling app ({CALENDAR}) that builds the roster within rules for skills, contract hours and rest times, the worker checks the roster and publishes it, and swaps are requested and approved in the same app. New staff take the theory of safety and procedures as online modules ({LMS}) before their first shift, so in-person training covers practice. Assigning duties and supervising stay with the worker; the app does not allocate shifts by behaviour or rate staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters were built in spreadsheets, swaps went through message groups and all training was in person.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling apps handle availability and swaps; learning systems deliver short modules.
tasks.still_hard: Seasonal staff join at short notice.
tasks.human_edge: Matching a quiet new staff member with a patient colleague.

evidence.claim: Scheduling apps build rosters from availability and handle swaps; learning systems deliver short modules.
Apps that time-stamp each staff action can monitor performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff availability to swaps handled; hiring is outside.
Input contract: availability from staff; modules from the employer; fallback is spreadsheets and in-person training.

Assigning, supervising, checking and publishing the roster keep their full time. s1 keeps 40 because the worker still adjusts the proposed roster. s3 keeps 85 because only the theory moves to modules; practice stays in person. s5 keeps 40 because the app checks skills and rest rules and the worker approves each swap.
Staff enter availability (s0, share 1) in about the time a message took; this and new staff's module time are outside the worker's savings.

incremental.description: Recreation worker keeps roster rules current.

approvals.approved_version: The roster exactly as checked by the worker in s1c, published once to the staff of this team in the scheduling app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small stable team whose roster hardly changes and few new staff (9.1); high: many seasonal staff and a roster rebuilt each week (17.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Inspect recreation areas and facilities, collect participant feedback, tally attendance and feedback, judge whether services produce the desired results, write the evaluation note, and send it to the manager.

steps.what: Recreation worker evaluates recreation areas and facilities on site
Participants fill in the short online survey after their visit
Recreation worker collects participant feedback: on paper forms today; after the change shows the QR code and hands paper forms to those without a phone
Recreation worker tallies attendance and feedback in a spreadsheet
Recreation worker judges whether services are producing desired results
Recreation worker writes the evaluation note
Recreation worker checks the final note: the figures match the dashboard, the judgement reads as meant, and it goes to the manager
Recreation worker sends the checked note to the manager

tasks.design: Participants get a short online survey by QR code or after-visit e-mail from the booking system ({OTHER}) instead of paper forms, and a dashboard ({BI}) shows attendance and survey results per activity. The evaluation note uses a template with the dashboard figures. Inspecting areas and judging results stay with the worker. The worker checks the final note and sends it to the manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Feedback was on paper and attendance tallied by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking systems send surveys and feed dashboards.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing why a well-attended activity still disappoints people.
tasks.altitude: The worker reads figures instead of tallying them.

evidence.claim: Booking systems can send surveys and feed attendance dashboards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the evaluation period to the note sent; budget decisions are outside.
Input contract: attendance in the booking system; fallback is paper forms and tallies.
Participants fill the online survey (s2p, share 1) in about the time a paper form took; this is customer time outside the worker's savings.

Inspecting, judging, checking the note and sending it keep their full time. s2 keeps 30 for showing the code and handing out paper forms. s3 keeps 20 for reading the dashboard and adding paper forms. s5 keeps 70 because the template fills the figures; the worker still writes the evaluation.
research_questions: Does the survey response rate hold up online?

incremental.description: Recreation worker sets up surveys per activity.

approvals.approved_version: The evaluation note exactly as checked by the worker in s5c, sent once to the recreation manager; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few participants answer online, so paper forms and hand tallies stay for most (15.4); high: most participants answer online (29.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The recreation worker keeps instructing, directing events, supervising staff and judging services; paper lists, spreadsheet rosters and hand tallies shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the booking and scheduling systems
role.ambitious_version: A worker with more time with participants.
